What the colors selected in the viewer will do. Smart Select BG Color: Selects BG color and performs a histogram analysis to create a better initial matte Clean BG Noise: Clean the noise from the background Clean FG Noise: Clean the noise from the foreground Matte Sponge: Use to set pixels as completely foreground Make FG Trans: Used to suppress spill in foreground transparency Restore Detail: Bring back detail from the foreground, adding to the matte Spill Sponge: Use on transition edges to bring in the foreground matte Spill +/-: Doesn't affect the matte, use to remove color spill from foreground Matte +/-: Use to increase/decrease the matte density of the foreground matte Detail +/-: A more fine grained version of the Restore Detail operation Fine Tuning: Pick average color for fine tuning 3D Sample: Just pick colors to show in Primatte viewer Simple Select BG Color: Select the initial BG color

Determines what the output should be from the node. composite: Premults the foreground with the background based on the matte created premultiplied: Premults the foreground based on the matte created unpremultiplied: Output the values calculated by Primatte without premultiplying with the matte not premultiplied: Output the original foreground pixels along with the calculated matte adjust lighting FG: Output the calculated foreground with adjusted lighting applied adjust lighting BG: Output the calculated background used in adjusted lighting hybrid core: Output only the core matte created before compositing with the hybrid edge hybrid edge: Output only the edge matte created before compositing with the hybrid core

description.plain_text: A Primatte key is created incrementally by sampling pixels and boxes from the foreground image to control the polyhedron in colorspace that determines what pixels are in/outside the matte. To use, set the "operation" to how you want to use the color samples, or use the left/right arrow buttons to step through all the operations. Then use Ctrl+click or Ctrl+shift+drag to select color or boxes of color from the viewer. These are then used by the operation to adjust the polyhedron. NUKE provides unlimited Undo during this process. Primatte is a trademark of IMAGICA Corp. Primatte patent is held by IMAGICA Corp.

To use, set the "operation" to how you want to use the color samples, or use the left/right arrow buttons to step through all the operations. Then use Ctrl+click or Ctrl+shift+drag to select color or boxes of color from the viewer. These are then used by the operation to adjust the polyhedron. NUKE provides unlimited Undo during this process.
